Subject: Temp repurpose request: reserved slice for AcuityHealth pilot

Hi team,

Quick ask from Growth/Product: AcuityHealth (large regional provider) just committed to a 6-week pilot that starts Aug 3rd. They need consistent low-latency inference for live provider-assist use — estimated 120k tokens/day at peak. Sales is asking if we can temporarily repurpose ~20% of the dedicated slice currently reserved for the "Atlas" pilot to support Acuity's traffic for the pilot window (6 weeks).

Why this matters: Acuity is a high strategic motion — they’ve indicated enterprise procurement will likely convert to Dedicated if pilot performance is solid. We have two constraints: SLA for Atlas (soft 99th latency target) and the autoscaling policy that prevents burst allocations beyond reserved capacity without an exception.

What I need from you:
- Kimberly: product risks / customer-facing SLO question and prioritization guidance.
- Marcus: infra feasibility — what does repurposing 20% of the slice look like operationally? Can we carve safely for 6 weeks without violating Autoscale guardrails?
- Laura: commercial — any contract or billing gating (discount/commitment changes) we should flag?

Attachments: acuity-pilot-onepager.pdf (one-pager sent to customer), capacity-impact.xlsx (basic token/slot estimates).

Proposed mitigations I’m open to: a) true repurpose (reserve reassign for 6 weeks), b) temporary burst-lane with an autoscale exception, c) hybrid (dedicated carve + strict rate-limits).

Timing: Sales needs an answer by EOD Thu (7/22) so please respond with feasibility and preferred option.

Thanks,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior GTM Programs Manager | Redwood Inference

Rafael — thanks for the context and attachments. A few product notes up front:

- Atlas SLA: user-facing latency 99th must stay <= 450ms; throughput fluctuation up to +/-15% is tolerable for short windows if we can schedule mitigation.
- Can we get a target max qps and expected simultaneous sessions per minute from Acuity? 120k tokens/day is helpful but we need traffic shape to validate tail risk.

Operational asks from product:
1) Clear guardrail on fallback: if Atlas 99th slips more than 10% for >30m, we should have an automated rollback to original allocation (no manual delays).
2) Observability: need per-customer route-level tracing and token-level cost delta reported in Console (preferably a temp dashboard).
3) Duration: pilot start Aug 3 — is the 6-week window fixed? If it shortens, we should not request structural slice changes.

Preference wise, I favor option b) temporary burst-lane + autoscale exception since it minimizes long-term config churn, but only if Marcus confirms no risk of prolonged interference. If infra says repurpose (option a) is low friction, we can support that as well if billing is straightforward.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park

Short answer: feasible, with caveats and a preferred approach.

What repurposing 20% looks like (infra):
- The Atlas slice is a 40-GPU pool (logical). 20% == 8 GPUs. Carving those out for 6 weeks would require: reallocation at the scheduler layer, updating placement constraints, and a short rolling restart of affected pods (impact window ~3-5 minutes).
- Autoscale policy: current policy prevents automated burst beyond reserved without a signed exception; we can grant a temporary exception scoped to the Acuity route only and bounded by concurrency/QPS caps. That avoids reassigning the slice globally.
- Risk: if Acuity traffic spikes unexpectedly for >2 hours, we risk knocking Atlas tail latency above the 10% degradation threshold. We can mitigate with strict token QPS throttles, and an automated route-level fallback that sends Acuity requests to a less-optimized but compatible model variant.

Recommended path (least operational risk):
1) Create an Acuity-specific burst lane (temporary autoscale exception) with hard caps (max 8 GPUs worth of burst, per-minute QPS caps) — no persistent topology changes required.
2) Implement automated rollback trigger: monitor Atlas 99th and if >10% degradation for 30m, immediately revoke burst lanes and direct Acuity to model-variant fallback.
3) Provision a 1-hour oncall window for the Aug 3 ramp day with infra + product + sales on standby.

I opened INF-4187 for the exception gating and added a draft runbook. See: https://jira.redwood/INF-4187.

Attachments: capacity-impact.xlsx (I updated sheet 'infra_notes' with GPU mapping and impact rows).

Marcus

Thanks all — summary and next steps below (aiming to keep this short so Sales can communicate to Acuity).

Decision: proceed with Marcus' recommended approach (option b: Acuity-specific burst lane + autoscale exception) with the controls listed. This preserves Atlas topology and minimizes long-term config changes.

Key controls we agreed on:
- Burst cap: up to 8 GPUs equivalent, scoped to Acuity route only.
- Throttles: conservative per-minute token/QPS caps per capacity-impact.xlsx (Marcus updated).
- Rollback: automated revoke if Atlas 99th latency > 10% for >30m. Infra to implement immediately.
- Observability: Product to request a temporary dashboard with per-route latency and token cost (Kim to own).
- Oncall: 1-hour staffed window on Aug 3 09:00-10:00 PT (Marcus + Kim + Rafael).
- Commercial: Laura, please confirm whether this requires a short-term amendment to the pilot MSA or a PO change; Sales needs the wording for contract.

Action items and owners:
- Marcus: finalize INF-4187 runbook, implement autoscale exception, and confirm rollback automation by 7/30.
- Kimberly: spin up a temporary route dashboard and confirm SLO instrumentation by 7/30.
- Laura: confirm commercial gating and any billing/pricing notes by 7/28.
- Rafael: I'll notify Acuity and update HubSpot with the plan + link to INF-4187.

@Alice / Acuity team — we will aim to have the infra and product controls in place before your Aug 3 start. If you can share a simple traffic-shape CSV (peak sessions per minute + median token per request) that will let us validate the throttles.
